title: market channel — schema-first (AFB backend<->AFB frontend only; not part of afb.execution.v1 wire)
description: Negotiated via auth.support/auth_ok.support (capability id afbws.market.channel.v1). Replaces the legacy `candles` channel (klines + background datasets positions/trades/hhi/orders), `stream/favorites`, `stream/positions`, and `securities/marketdata|futures|positions` for clients that negotiated this capability; legacy stays available as fallback for clients that did not — this migration carries no version-gated behaviour, negotiation is purely by `auth.support`/`auth_ok.support`. Every instrument is addressed by the catalog's full `instrument_key` (see common.v1.json#/$defs/instrumentKey), not a bare SECID. Two data templates cover all payload shapes: `series` (candles and every background dataset, keyed by `time`) and `snapshot` (a cross-instrument slice, keyed by `instrument_key`), both columnar (`$defs/table`: `columns` + `rows`). The same schema id serves both as the reply to a `get` (carries `request_id`) and as an unsolicited push to a live subscription (no `request_id`) — deliberately no `.request`/`.response`/`.push` suffix on schema ids. Every data message carries `received_at` (when AFB received the data from its source) and `tz` (the trading venue's IANA zone that row-level `time`/day boundaries are aligned to). Subscriptions (`subscribe`) are explicit and replace-all: the client states its whole desired `snapshot`/`series` scope every time, the server does not diff against a previous statement. `NaN` never appears on the wire — sources that produce it are converted to `null`. See AFB/docs/ws/market.md.

table.title: Columnar data block for one dataset `kind`.
table.description: `rows` are keyed by their first column: `time` (UTC unix seconds) for the series kinds (candles/positions/trades/hhi/orders), `instrument_key` for the snapshot kinds (quote/oi/oi_daily). Beyond that first column, `columns` may list any subset of the kind's allowed fields in any order — a client reads by column name, never by positional index — so the server can add a field later without a schema bump, as long as it stays inside the per-kind enum below. `rows` elements are `number | string | null`; a source value that is NaN is sent as `null`, never as the string "NaN" or JSON NaN.

rows.description: Each row has the same length and column order as `columns`.

seriesTableEntry.title: One `series.tables[]` element: `#/$defs/table` restricted to the series kinds.

snapshotTableEntry.title: One `snapshot.tables[]` element: `#/$defs/table` restricted to the snapshot kinds.

series.title: afbws.market.series.v1 — one instrument's candles or one background dataset.
series.description: Reply to `get` (target=series) when `request_id` is present; unsolicited push to a live series subscription when it is absent.

tz.description: IANA timezone of the trading venue (e.g. "Europe/Moscow") that bar boundaries and trading-day edges are aligned to. Not the client's local timezone.

received_at.description: When AFB received this data from its source (broker/cache), ISO-8601 with offset. Distinct from the row-level `time` (UTC unix seconds), which is when the bar/event itself occurred.

mode.description: "replace": this is the full answer to a `get` — the client replaces its local copy of this instrument+period+kind range with `tables`. "merge": this is a live push — the client upserts `tables` rows by `time` into its existing copy (the latest bar, or dataset catch-up).

from.description: Start of the range actually covered by `tables`, YYYY-MM-DD in `tz`.

to.description: End of the range actually covered by `tables`, YYYY-MM-DD in `tz`.

source.description: Where this data came from, when known.

message.description: Optional human-readable note (e.g. partial coverage, provider fallback).

snapshot.title: afbws.market.snapshot.v1 — cross-instrument slice (quote / oi / oi_daily).
snapshot.description: Reply to `get` (target=snapshot) when `request_id` is present; unsolicited push to a live snapshot subscription when it is absent.

tz.description: IANA timezone of the trading venue, used to align `oi_daily`'s midnight `time` to the trading day.

received_at.description: When AFB received this data from its source, ISO-8601 with offset.

mode.description: "full": the complete answer to a `get`, or the initial push right after `subscribe` — the client replaces its local snapshot for the accepted scope. "update": a live push carrying only the rows that changed since the last full/update.

subscriptionSnapshotSpec.title: Snapshot subscription scope, as requested by the client or echoed back as accepted.

subscriptionSeriesSpec.title: One series subscription entry (one instrument+period), as requested by the client or echoed back as accepted.

subscribe.title: afbws.market.subscribe.v1 — replace-all subscription statement (client -> server).
subscribe.description: The client states its whole desired subscription scope every time; the server does not diff against a previous `subscribe`. An empty body — neither `snapshot` nor `series` present — unsubscribes from everything. Reply is `subscription` with the same `request_id`, immediately followed by a `snapshot` push with `mode:"full"` for the accepted snapshot scope.

subscription.title: afbws.market.subscription.v1 — accepted subscription state, reply to subscribe.v1.
subscription.description: `snapshot`/`series` are the accepted subset of what was requested (same shapes as subscribe.v1); `rejected` lists instrument keys that could not be resolved/subscribed, with a reason code. Always followed by a `snapshot` push with `mode:"full"` for the accepted snapshot scope.

get.title: afbws.market.get.v1 — one-shot request (client -> server).
get.description: Reply is `series` (target=series) or `snapshot` (target=snapshot) with the same `request_id`, or `error`.

start_date.description: target=series only: first date to fetch, YYYY-MM-DD in the instrument's market tz.

end_date.description: target=series only: last date to fetch, YYYY-MM-DD; omitted means up to the latest available.

base.description: target=series only: opaque provider/period hint (candle base), passed through unchanged.

instrument_keys.description: target=snapshot only: instruments to fetch; omitted means every instrument with cached data (used by TickersList).
